nindian-history-132-12.s: Which of the following movements came earliest?
nindian-history-132-12.x: The Home Rule Movement began in 1916, before Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Quit India (1942).

n40bc4d14722.s: Who resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
n40bc4d14722.x: C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council; Tagore renounced his Knighthood and Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.

n07fc8a550a8.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 was India's first all-India:
n07fc8a550a8.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first all-India mass strike and was urban-centred, not confined to rural Punjab.

nindian-history-100-17.s: In which year was the Poona Pact signed?
nindian-history-100-17.x: The Poona Pact came in September 1932, after the Dandi March (1930) and the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931), and before Quit India (1942).

new.s: Gandhi wanted untouchability removed through reform:
new.x: Gandhi called untouchability a blot on Hinduism and sought reform from within Hindu society.

new.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was earlier known as the:
new.x: The Sangh's former name was the All India Anti-Untouchability League.

new.s: Who served as secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
new.x: Thakkar Bapa was the secretary; G.D. Birla was its first president.

new.s: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh, while in prison, on:
new.x: The Sangh was founded on 30 September 1932, after the Poona Pact.

new.s: Gandhi's Harijan tour of November 1933 – July 1934 covered about:
new.x: The Harijan tour covered about 20,000 km and raised funds for the Sangh.

new.s: Gandhi began his Harijan tour of 1933-34 from:
new.x: The Harijan tour started from Wardha Ashram in November 1933.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25)?
new.x: Vaikom was led by T.K. Madhavan, K. Kelappan and K.P. Kesava Menon; Potti Sriramulu led the Nellore temple-entry fasts of 1946.

new.s: During the Guruvayur Satyagraha, Gandhi persuaded whom to end his fast in 1932?
new.x: K. Kelappan led the Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931-32); Gandhi persuaded him to end his fast.

new.s: The temple-entry fasts of 1946 in Nellore were undertaken by:
new.x: Potti Sriramulu undertook the Nellore temple-entry fasts in 1946.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's views on women:
1. He opposed purdah and child marriage.
2. He opposed dowry.
3. He opposed the remarriage of child widows.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Gandhi opposed purdah, child marriage and dowry; statement 3 is wrong as he supported the remarriage of child widows.

new.s: Durgabai met Gandhi in 1921 and raised Rs 5,000 at:
new.x: Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921 and raised Rs 5,000.

new.s: Kolla Tayaramma ran Harijan schools and hostels at:
new.x: Kolla Tayaramma worked at Tenali; Alladi Annapurna Devi ran Harijan schools at Nellore.

new.s: For Gandhi, the bedrock of Indian nationalism was:
new.x: Gandhi regarded Hindu-Muslim unity as the bedrock of nationalism and backed the Khilafat cause for it.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's religious outlook:
1. Sarva dharma samabhava means equal respect for all religions.
2. His ashram prayers drew on many faiths.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: sarva dharma samabhava is equal respect for all religions, and the ashram prayers drew on many faiths.

new.s: The Wardha Scheme of Basic Education (1937) was drawn up by the:
new.x: The Wardha Scheme, adopted at the Wardha Educational Conference of 1937, was drawn up by the Zakir Hussain Committee.

new.s: The Wardha Scheme proposed free and compulsory education for:
new.x: Basic education was to be free and compulsory for 7 years, from age 7 to 14.

new.s: Under Nai Talim, the medium of instruction was to be the:
new.x: Nai Talim called for teaching in the mother tongue, with learning through a productive craft.

new.s: On his Harijan tour, Gandhi spoke at Mogalrajpuram, Vijayawada on:
new.x: Gandhi spoke at Mogalrajpuram, Vijayawada on 16 December 1933 during the Harijan tour.

new.s: Gandhi's tour of Andhra in 1933 was mainly to:
o: collect funds and campaign against untouchability
set up the Wardha Scheme schools
new.x: He toured Andhra on the Harijan tour to collect funds and campaign against untouchability.

new.s: Gandhi's Tolstoy Farm (1910) in South Africa was near:
new.x: Tolstoy Farm (1910) was near Johannesburg; the Phoenix Settlement (1904) was near Durban.

new.s: Gandhi set up the Phoenix Settlement near Durban in:
new.x: The Phoenix Settlement was founded in 1904; Gandhi reached South Africa in 1893 and set up Tolstoy Farm in 1910.

new.s: Gandhi's first major public speech in India was delivered in February 1916 at:
new.x: His first major public speech in India was at BHU in February 1916.

new.s: Who first called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'?
new.x: Subhas Chandra Bose gave the title 'Father of the Nation'; Tagore gave 'Mahatma'.

new.s: Gandhi's autobiography is titled:
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
new.x: His autobiography is The Story of My Experiments with Truth; Hind Swaraj is another of his writings and Unto This Last is Ruskin's.

new.s:
Arrange Gandhi's ashrams in the order they were founded:
1. Sevagram, Wardha
2. Satyagraha Ashram, Kochrab
3. Sabarmati Ashram
new.x: Kochrab came in 1915, Sabarmati in 1917 and Sevagram in 1936.

new.s: The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) is known as Gandhi's first:
new.x: Kheda was the first non-cooperation; Champaran the first civil disobedience and Ahmedabad the first hunger strike.

new.s: Gandhi reached Champaran on:
new.x: Gandhi reached Champaran on 10 April 1917 with Brajkishore Prasad, Rajendra Prasad and others.

new.s: In Champaran, 'Sharahbeshi' meant:
new.x: Sharahbeshi was enhanced rent; tawan was lump-sum compensation and tinkathia the 3/20th indigo obligation.

new.s: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918), the mill owners were led by:
new.x: Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners; his sister Anusuya Sarabhai stood with the workers.

new.s: How long did the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 last?
new.x: The strike lasted 21 days, not 35; 35% was the wage rise awarded.

new.s: The Ahmedabad mill dispute of 1918 began when the owners withdrew the:
new.x: The mill owners withdrew the plague bonus, and workers demanded a 50% wage rise.

new.s: Besides Vallabhbhai Patel, the organisers of the Kheda Satyagraha included:
new.x: Patel, Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh organised Kheda, with Gandhi as spiritual head.

new.s: Gandhi formed the Satyagraha Sabha against the Rowlatt Act on 24 February 1919 at:
new.x: The Satyagraha Sabha was organised at Bombay on 24 February 1919; members took an oath to disobey the Act.

new.s: Under the Rowlatt Act, political suspects could be detained without trial for up to:
new.x: The Act allowed detention without trial for up to two years, with trials by three High Court judges and no appeal.

new.s: At Jallianwala Bagh, Dyer's troops fired about how many rounds in some 10 minutes?
new.x: About 1,650 rounds were fired in around 10 minutes; 379 dead and 1,100 injured were the official figures.

new.s: Gandhi was tried for sedition in March 1922 ('The Great Trial') at:
new.x: Gandhi was tried at Ahmedabad on 18 March 1922.

new.s: The judge who sentenced Gandhi in the sedition trial of 1922 was:
new.x: Judge Broomfield sentenced Gandhi to six years, following Tilak's case.

new.s: The sedition charge against Gandhi in 1922 rested on three articles in:
new.x: The charge was based on three Young India articles, including 'Tampering with Loyalty' and 'Shaking the Manes'.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's sedition trial of 1922:
1. He was arrested at his ashram on 10 March 1922.
2. He pleaded not guilty.
3. The printer Shankerlal Banker got one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 and Banker got one year; statement 2 is wrong as Gandhi pleaded guilty.

new.s: The Moplah Revolt of 1921 took place in:
new.x: The Moplah Revolt (1921) was a rising of the Mappila Muslims of Malabar, Kerala.

new.s: Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr Satyapal were arrested on:
new.x: They were arrested on 9 April 1919, not 13 April, the day of the massacre.

new.s: The crawling order applied to the Amritsar lane where ____ had been assaulted.
new.x: Indians had to crawl through the lane where the English missionary Marcella Sherwood had been assaulted.

new.s: After 13 April 1919, martial law was imposed in Amritsar and:
new.x: Martial law was imposed in Amritsar and Lahore under O'Dwyer's regime.

new.s: C. Sankaran Nair later lost a libel suit brought by:
new.x: Sankaran Nair lost Michael O'Dwyer's libel suit by an 11-1 verdict.

new.s: The Hunter Committee was officially called the:
new.x: The Hunter Committee was the Disorders Inquiry Committee, set up on 14 October 1919.

new.s: How many of the Hunter Committee's eight members were Indians?
new.x: It had 8 members: 5 British and 3 Indian.

new.s: The minority report of the Hunter Committee, more critical of Dyer, was written by:
new.x: Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan wrote the minority report; the five British members wrote the majority report.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Congress's Punjab Sub-Committee?
new.x: Setalvad was an Indian member of the official Hunter Committee; the Congress committee had Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Tyabji, Jayakar and Gandhi.

new.s: Abbas Tyabji was a member of the:
new.x: Abbas Tyabji sat on the Congress's non-official Punjab Sub-Committee.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Congress inquiry into the Punjab events:
1. It called the firing inhuman.
2. It described Dyer's action as 'an error of judgement'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Congress report called the firing inhuman; 'an error of judgement' was the Hunter Committee's verdict.

new.s: Which of the following was an outcome of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
new.x: After the massacre faith in British justice declined; the other events came before it.

new.s: The Sedition (Rowlatt) Committee, whose report led to the Rowlatt Act, was appointed in:
new.x: The Sedition Committee under Justice Sidney Rowlatt was appointed in 1917.

new.s: Which Andhra newspapers opposed the Rowlatt Act?
new.x: Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika opposed the Act.

new.s: Which of the following events took place in 1920?
new.x: Tilak died on 1 August 1920; the Lucknow Pact was 1916, the Moplah Revolt 1921 and the Simon Commission 1928.
